key_insight: A unified analysis shows how modern optimizers trade off convergence speed, generalization, and computational (and privacy) costs across practical scenarios—providing a structured evaluation framework and actionable guidance for optimizer choice.
problem_solved: Helps practitioners and researchers navigate the complexity of selecting and configuring optimization methods for large-scale training, differential privacy constraints, and distributed/hardware-constrained settings where conventional SGD/Adam choices reveal important limitations.
method: Survey and taxonomy of optimization algorithms (SGD, Adam-family, adaptive and hybrid methods) mapped to real-world scenarios (large models, DP training, distributed/hardware-aware pipelines).
A unified evaluation framework and empirical benchmark suite that measures convergence, generalization, computational efficiency, and privacy–utility tradeoffs across scenarios.
Synthesis of practical guidelines and hyperparameter heuristics for optimizer selection and tuning under different constraints.
impact: Provides clear, scenario-aware guidance that reduces trial-and-error when building training pipelines—enabling more efficient, privacy-compliant, and scalable model training across ML systems and hardware stacks.
visual_elements: Trade-off triangle (convergence speed vs generalization vs compute/energy) plotting common optimizers at representative positions.
Benchmark heatmap matrix: optimizers (rows) × scenarios (columns) colored by combined performance metric (convergence, accuracy, compute, privacy).
Decision flowchart for optimizer selection based on priorities (privacy budget, dataset size, hardware limits, communication cost).
Bar/line chart illustrating privacy–utility–cost curves (e.g., DP noise vs accuracy vs runtime) for select optimizers.
paper_title: Evolution of Optimization Methods: Algorithms, Scenarios, and Evaluations
paper_authors: Tong Zhang, Jiangning Zhang, Zhucun Xue, Juntao Jiang, Yicheng Xu
